operationalSituations.description: Normal vehicle operation — all RC Server endpoints reachable
Partial network fault — one or more RC Server endpoints unreachable
Safety-critical manoeuvre — emergency braking or collision avoidance active
HPC software fault — runaway process, crash, or OOM condition
Elevated network latency — congestion, EMI, or hardware degradation
Adversarial access — attacker present on the RCP Ethernet network

hazards.description: Loss of request delivery to a safety-critical endpoint (e.g. braking actuator)
Spurious request delivered to the wrong endpoint (wrong avtp.ByteBusID within a stream)
RC Server watchdog liveness kick not delivered, leading to unintended safe-state entry or reset
Delayed request delivery — endpoint responds within the protocol timeout but too slowly for real-time control
Corrupted request/response payload — bit error or memory fault causes a wrong actuator value to be applied
Endpoint impersonation — a rogue device spoofs a legitimate avtp.StreamID and accepts or intercepts requests
HPC crash without graceful shutdown — RC Server endpoints remain active with no watchdog kicks, entering an indeterminate state
Priority inversion — a high-priority request (per request.Kind's server-derived ordering, e.g. an emergency-brake write) blocked behind lower-priority requests under load
Request flooding — a runaway HPC software loop overwhelms an RC Server endpoint, causing it to drop safety-critical requests
Request replay — an attacker retransmits a previously captured valid request in a new vehicle context, causing unintended actuation

safetyGoals.description: The RCP library shall detect and report request delivery failures within the timeout period.
The RCP library shall validate that responses are addressed to the requesting endpoint and reject mismatched deliveries.
The RCP library shall provide a periodic watchdog liveness mechanism (e2e.Supervisor) and ensure a missed kick is detected within the configured watchdog timeout.
Maximum end-to-end request latency shall be bounded and monitored; a violation shall be reported as a health event.
Request and response payloads shall be integrity-protected using a CRC32 safe-point mechanism (e2e); frames failing the check shall be rejected.

Endpoint identity (avtp.StreamID) shall be authenticated before requests are accepted; an unauthenticated response shall be rejected. (Open per TARA.md T-RCP-001 — this repository does not implement StreamID authentication; see iso21434/tara.go.)
RC Servers shall detect cessation of watchdog kicks and enter a defined safe state within the configured watchdog timeout (e2e.Supervisor).
A high-priority request (per request.Kind's server-derived ordering) shall never be delayed by a lower-priority request in any queue or admission-control mechanism.
The HPC shall enforce per-endpoint request rate limits (ratelimit); requests exceeding the rate limit shall be rejected before reaching the RC Server.
Requests shall carry a monotonically increasing sequence per the e2e safe-point mechanism; frames whose sequence falls outside the anti-replay window shall be rejected.
